exercises.prompt: Identify the Cyrillic letter that represents the bilabial nasal consonant /m/ (equivalent in visual shape to Latin 'M').
exercises.hint: Look for the letter identical in form to the English uppercase 'M'.

options.explanation: Correct! Cyrillic 'М' represents /m/ and shares its glyph form with Latin 'M'.
Incorrect. 'И' represents the vowel /i/, which looks like a reversed 'N'.
Incorrect. 'П' represents the voiceless stop /p/ (Greek Pi).

exercises.explanation: Cyrillic uppercase 'М' and lowercase 'м' represent the voiced bilabial nasal consonant /m/. It is visually identical to Latin 'M'.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Маш сайн! You correctly recognized Cyrillic 'М'.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Remember, Cyrillic 'М' looks identical to the Latin letter 'M'.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Modern Mongolian Cyrillic shares several glyphs directly with Latin: A, O, M, T, K. Consonant 'М' corresponds to the universal bilabial nasal phoneme [m].

exercises.exerciseTitle: Matching Lowercase and Uppercase Shared Consonants
exercises.prompt: Pair each uppercase Cyrillic letter with its exact lowercase partner for the shared letters Т, К, О, А.
exercises.hint: Cyrillic lowercase letters generally mirror their uppercase shapes in reduced height.
exercises.explanation: In printed Cyrillic, letters like Т, К, О, and А have identical letterforms in uppercase and lowercase, varying only in font size.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Зөв! All case pairings match correctly.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Check each letter: Т-т, К-к, О-о, А-а.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Unlike Latin handwriting where cursive 't' differs substantially from 'T', Mongolian Cyrillic print preserves the uniform bar top for both uppercase Т and lowercase т.

exercises.prompt: Which of the following common Mongolian loanwords begins with the shared Cyrillic consonant 'К'?
exercises.hint: Think of the international word for cinema / movie.
exercises.explanation: Cyrillic 'К' appears predominantly in international loanwords in Mongolian such as 'кино' (movie), 'карт' (card), and 'кофе' (coffee).

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Сайн байна! 'кино' is spelled with initial Cyrillic 'к'.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Native Mongolian vocabulary uses 'г' and 'х' for velar and uvular stops/fricatives. The letter 'к' was introduced into the Cyrillic orthography primarily to accommodate 20th-century Russian and international loan vocabulary.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the scrambled letters to spell the classical cultural word 'тамга' (seal/stamp), observing the shared consonants Т, М, and vowel А.
exercises.contextSentence: Төрийн сүлд тамга (State seal and stamp)
exercises.hint: The word starts with 'т', followed by 'а' and 'м'.
exercises.explanation: Т-а-м-г-а spells 'тамга' (seal, stamp). It contains shared consonants т and м along with back vowel а.

learnerFeedback.onFailure: Follow the sequence: т -> а -> м -> г -> а.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: 'Тамга' is a historical and cultural term designating sovereign stamps, clan seals, and brand marks throughout Central Asia.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the spoken audio and type the two-letter word with shared consonant Т: 'то' or 'та'?
exercises.hint: Listen for the open low back vowel /a/ after /tʰ/.
exercises.explanation: The speaker pronounced 'та' (/tʰa/), which is also the formal second-person pronoun ('you').

learnerFeedback.onFailure: Listen closely to the audio: 'т' followed by 'а' -> 'та'.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: 'Та' functions both as an orthographic syllable demonstrating consonants Т and А and as the essential polite pronoun of address in Mongolian.

lessons.cyrillicTitle: Accurately discern minimal pairs such as ор (bed/place) vs өр (debt), and ус (water) vs үс (hair).

lessons.communicativeOutcome: Accurately discern minimal pairs such as ор (bed/place) vs өр (debt), and ус (water) vs үс (hair).
lessons.audioPurpose: Pristine acoustic contrast between Khalkha phonemes /ɔ/, /ɵ/, /ʊ/, /u/.

exercises.exerciseTitle: Auditory Minimal Pair Contrast: О vs Ө
exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio recording. Did the speaker pronounce back rounded vowel word 'мод' (tree/wood) or front rounded vowel word 'мөр' (shoulder/path)?
exercises.hint: Notice whether the vowel resonance sounds deep and guttural (О) or mid-front and rounded (Ө).

options.explanation: Correct! The speaker pronounced the front rounded vowel /ө/ in 'мөр'.
Incorrect. 'мод' contains the back rounded vowel /ɔ/.

exercises.explanation: Cyrillic 'Ө' represents the front mid-rounded vowel /ө/ [ɵ], contrasting with 'О' which represents the back low-mid rounded vowel [ɔ].

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Маш сайн! You distinguished the front vowel 'ө' in 'мөр'.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Listen to the tongue position: 'ө' is higher and forward compared to 'о'.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: The phonemic contrast between back /ɔ/ and front /ө/ is fundamental to Khalkha phonology and governs root vowel harmony throughout the language.

exercises.exerciseTitle: Auditory Discrimination: High Back 'У' vs High Front 'Ү'
exercises.prompt: Listen carefully to the audio stimulus. Which word was spoken: 'ус' (water) or 'үс' (hair)?
exercises.hint: The back vowel 'у' has a pharyngeal resonance /ʊ/, while 'ү' is a front close vowel /u/.

options.explanation: Correct! The audio features the retracted back vowel /ʊ/ in 'ус'.
Incorrect. 'үс' has a higher, fronted vowel quality /u/.

exercises.explanation: Mongolian 'ус' (/ʊs/) uses the back rounded vowel У, whereas 'үс' (/us/) uses the front close rounded vowel Ү.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Зөв! That was 'ус' (water) with back vowel У.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: The spoken token has a deeper back tongue position: 'ус'.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: In Mongolian linguistic terminology, 'у' belongs to the masculine vowels (эр эгшиг), while 'ү' belongs to the feminine vowels (эм эгшиг). Conflating them changes word meaning completely.

exercises.exerciseTitle: Phonetic Categorization: Sorting Spoken Roots by Vowel Backness
exercises.prompt: Listen to the word: 'сүү' (milk). Does it contain a Front (feminine) vowel or a Back (masculine) vowel?
exercises.hint: The letter 'ү' is written with a vertical tick through the center and sounds like high front /u/.

options.explanation: Correct! 'сүү' features the long front rounded vowel үү.
Incorrect. 'сүү' contains front vowel ү, not back vowel у.

exercises.explanation: 'Сүү' (milk) is formed with the long front vowel 'үү', placing it squarely in the feminine (front) harmonic class.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Маш сайн! 'Сүү' is an exemplary front-vowel root.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Remember: 'ү' belongs to the front (эм) vowel class.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Long vowels in Mongolian are orthographically represented by double letters (аа, ээ, оо, өө, уу, үүү). Their harmonic class matches their single counterpart.

exercises.exerciseTitle: Minimal Pair Dictation: Өдөр vs Үнэн
exercises.prompt: Listen to the word meaning 'day' and type the Cyrillic spelling using the front vowel Ө:
exercises.hint: Transcribe the mid-front rounded vowel 'ө' followed by alveolar stop 'д' and coda 'р'.
exercises.explanation: 'Өдөр' (/өдөр/ [ɵtər]) means 'day'. It exemplifies harmonic assimilation where both vowels are mid-front 'ө'.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Гайхалтай! You spelled 'өдөр' with exact Cyrillic letters.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Remember that the word for 'day' has front rounded vowels: 'өдөр'.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Non-initial vowels in Khalkha Mongolian undergo reduction, but orthography preserves the harmonic front vowel symbol 'ө'.

exercises.exerciseTitle: Auditory Identification: Detecting the Odd Vowel Out
exercises.prompt: Three of these words contain back vowels (эр эгшиг). Which word contains a FRONT vowel (эм эгшиг)?
exercises.hint: Listen for the unrounded front vowel 'э'.
exercises.explanation: 'Гэр' contains 'э', a front unrounded vowel. The other three words contain 'у', a back rounded vowel.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Яг зөв! 'Гэр' is the front-vowel word.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: 'гэр' has 'э' which is front; the others have 'у' which is back.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Front vowels in Mongolian are: э, ө, ү (and front variants of и). Back vowels are: а, о, у.

exercises.exerciseTitle: Categorizing Core Roots: Masculine vs Feminine
exercises.prompt: Select the correct harmonic classification for the root word 'гал' (fire).
exercises.hint: The vowel 'а' is a masculine back vowel.

options.explanation: Correct! 'гал' contains 'а', making it an 'эр үг' (masculine back-vowel word).
Incorrect. 'гал' does not have front vowels.

exercises.explanation: Because 'гал' contains the low back vowel 'а', it is classified as a masculine word (эр үг) and will take back-vowel suffixes (e.g. гал-аас, гал-ын).

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Маш сайн! 'Гал' is an эр үг.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: 'а' is a back masculine vowel, so 'гал' is an эр үг.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Vowel harmony (эгшиг зохицох ёс) is the golden rule of Mongolian morphology: back-vowel roots only take back-vowel suffixes, and front-vowel roots only take front-vowel suffixes.

exercises.prompt: Select ALL words below that belong to the FEMININE / FRONT vowel class (эм үг):
exercises.hint: Look for words containing э, ө, or ү.
exercises.explanation: Both 'гэр' (vowel э) and 'өвөл' (vowel ө) are feminine front-vowel words (эм үг). 'Ном' and 'ус' contain back masculine vowels.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Сайн байна! 'гэр' and 'өвөл' are both feminine words.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Check the vowels: 'э' and 'ө' are feminine; 'о' and 'у' are masculine.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Feminine words take front harmonic suffix allomorphs such as -ээр/-өөр/-үүр, while masculine words take -аар/-оор/-уур.

exercises.exerciseTitle: Detecting Harmonic Violations in Nonce Words
exercises.prompt: Which of the following hypothetical word roots VIOLATES Mongolian vowel harmony rules by mixing masculine and feminine vowels?
exercises.hint: A single native root cannot contain both 'а' (masculine) and 'э' (feminine).

options.explanation: Correct! Mixing back 'а' with front 'э' in a single stem is strictly prohibited by vowel harmony.

options.text: малгай (all back vowels: а, а, ай)

options.explanation: Incorrect. The neutral vowel 'и' can freely occur with back vowels.

exercises.explanation: Native Mongolian roots maintain strict vowel harmony: back vowels (а, о, у) never co-occur with front vowels (э, ө, ү). Therefore, '*мадэ' is impossible.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Яг зөв! '*мадэ' illegally mixes back 'а' and front 'э'.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Remember: Masculine and feminine vowels can never mix in a native root.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: The only exception to pure harmonic separation is the neutral vowel 'и', which may appear in both masculine and feminine words without changing the dominant gender of the root.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the tokens so that the two MASCULINE roots appear first, followed by the two FEMININE roots.
exercises.hint: 'нар' (sun) and 'сар' (moon) have vowel 'а' (masculine). 'гэр' and 'сүү' have front vowels (feminine).

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Төгс! Masculine (нар, сар) then feminine (гэр, сүү).
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Group by vowel: нар & сар are masculine; гэр & сүү are feminine.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: In Mongolian poetry and cosmology, 'нар сар' (sun and moon) are paired masculine celestial symbols, while 'гэр орон' anchors domestic life.

exercises.exerciseTitle: Auditory Identification of Root Gender Harmony
exercises.prompt: Listen to the word 'морь' (horse). Because it contains vowel 'о' with palatalized 'рь', what suffix set will it take?
exercises.hint: 'О' is a back masculine vowel with labial rounding.

options.text: Masculine suffixes with back harmony (e.g. -оор/-ын: мориор)
options.explanation: Correct! The root vowel 'о' dictates masculine rounded suffix harmony.

exercises.correctAnswer: Masculine suffixes with back harmony (e.g. -оор/-ын: мориор)
exercises.explanation: 'Морь' (/mɔrʲ/) has root vowel 'о'. The soft sign indicates palatalization of 'р', but the dominant vowel is 'о', demanding back masculine suffixes.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Яг зөв! 'Морь' takes masculine suffixes such as 'мориор'.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: The primary vowel is 'о', which is masculine.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Palatalization (зөөлний тэмдэг ь) affects consonant articulation but does not alter the fundamental back/front harmonic classification of the root vowel.

lessons.title: Mongolian Cyrillic Keyboard Layout & The Home Row
